summation.displayName: In quiescent cells, RAF is maintained in a closed state in w...
summation.text: In quiescent cells, RAF is maintained in a closed state in which the N-terminal regulatory region sterically blocks the catalytic region (Cutler et al, 1998; Tran et al, 2003; Terai et al, 2005; Tran et al, 2005; reviewed in Udell et al, 2011). This closed state is mediated in part by the intramolecular binding of YWHAB/14-3-3 dimers to two phosphorylated serine residues (S259 and S621 in RAF1, S214 and S582 in ARAF and S365 and S729 in BRAF) (Ory et al, 2003; Jaumot et al, 2001; Fischer et al, 2009; reviewed in Udell et al, 2011).
